items.abstract: <jats:p>The Abelian sandpile growth model is a diffusion process for configurations of chips placed on vertices of the integer lattice Zd, in which sites with at least 2d chips topple, distributing one chip to each of their neighbors in the lattice, until no more topplings are possible. From an initial configuration consisting of n chips placed at a single vertex, the rescaled stable configuration seems to converge to a particular fractal pattern as n→∞. However, little has been proved about the appearance of the stable configurations. We use partial differential equation techniques to prove that the rescaled stable configurations do indeed converge to a unique limit as n→∞. We characterize the limit as the Laplacian of the solution to an elliptic obstacle problem.</jats:p>
title: Convergence of the Abelian sandpile

items.abstract: <jats:p>We prove that Abelian sandpiles with random initial states converge almost surely to unique scaling limits. The proof follows the Armstrong–Smart program for stochastic homogenization of uniformly elliptic equations. Using simple random walk estimates, we prove an analogous result for the divisible sandpile and identify its scaling limit as exactly that of the averaged divisible sandpile. As a corollary, this gives a new quantitative proof of known results on the stabilizability of Abelian sandpiles.</jats:p>
title: Convergence of the random Abelian sandpile
